newsitem.title: LEBANON: Israeli planes hit Hizbollah targets in Lebanon.
newsitem.headline: Israeli planes hit Hizbollah targets in Lebanon.

text.p: Israeli planes raided suspected pro-Iranian Hizbollah positions in south Lebanon on Monday after the Moslem guerrillas wounded two Israel-backed militiamen, security sources said.
They said two planes fired a total of four rockets at the hills of the outskirts of Mashghara town, a Hizbollah stronghold on the southern tip of the eastern Syrian-controlled Bekaa valley.
There was no immediate word on casualties in the air attack -- the 36th into Lebanon since the beginning of 1997.
Two hours earlier, two pro-Israeli South Lebanon Army (SLA) militiamen were wounded when Hizbollah fighters detonated a roadside bomb near the town of Jizzine, SLA sources said.
Jizzine is a strip of territory officially outside Israel's south Lebanon occupation zone but under SLA control.
The sources said the bomb went off as an SLA armoured car was on its way to the militia's position in Tomat Niha The vehicle was destroyed, they said.
In Jerusalem, an Israeli army statement said the SLA men were in an operational activity when they were wounded and the Israeli air raid was a retaliation to the bomb attack.
"Two SLA soldiers were lightly wounded this afternoon by a roadside bomb explosion in Jizzine area while they were on operational activity," the statement said.

"At the same time, an anti-tank missile was fired at the force and (Israeli) air force therefore attacked terrorist targets in the Jizzine area in the eastern sector of the security zone. The planes hit their targets and returned safely to base," it added.
The security sources said Israeli troops shelled the areas close to Mashghara with heavy artillary but no casualties were reported.
Hizbollah (Party of God) guerrillas regularly attack Israeli troops and the SLA in a bid to oust them from the 15-km (nine miles)-wide occupation zone.
